COMMON ORDER

These petitions are filed seeking quashment of the FIR in Crime No.1947 of 2011 on the file of the 1st respondent police registered against the petitioners in both petitions for the offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 341, 294(b), 465, 420 and 506(i) IPC.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD) No.13701 of 2022 & 51 of 2023 2.Since these petitions are filed seeking quashment of the very same FIR, these petitions are heard together and disposed of by this common order.

3.During the course of the submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioners in both the petitions submitted that the defacto complainant and the petitioners have settled the matter out of the Court and the defacto complainant has given a representation to the respondent Police to close the further proceedings.
4.The learned counsel for the defacto complainant has submitted that compromise talks are still not concluded.

5.The learned Government Advocate (Crl.side) for the 1st respondent in both the petitions, on the other hand, has submitted that if both the petitioners and the defacto complainant file representations before the Investigating Officer, the same will be considered and closed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD) No.13701 of 2022 & 51 of 2023

6.Considering the submissions made on either side, these Criminal Original Petitions are disposed of, directing the petitioners and the defacto complainant to submit their respective representations Ochubalu vs The State Rep.

By on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10350584/
2 to the respondent Police, within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order,
on which, the respondent Police are directed to consider and dispose of the same within a period of two weeks thereafter.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
